history.by: U2b: first run (content-order extraction, B9d): every -ordered file scores 1.000; the -reversed files lose order (0.000-0.333) and keep their text, except table-reversed (text 0.572: cells drawn right to left on one baseline are joined without a space, an extraction bug left for a B9 follow-up)
B9e: a separator where the pen jumps back on a line; table-reversed keeps every cell's words (text 0.572 → 1.000), no other file changes

T3b: the corpus grows from 22 files to 28 with three hard layouts (pull-quote, narrow-gutter, wrapped-grid), drawn both ways; the content-order score of the files already there doesn't change, so the mean moves only because the set does

U4c: first run of the approximate reader mode (layout order, figures and tables as crops, low-confidence pages as images with their text kept): every file but the three hard layouts scores 1.000; narrow-gutter (0.545), pull-quote (0.714) and wrapped-grid (0.700) lose order as extraction's layout order does, and no file trails copy as paragraph; 6 pages (the hard layouts' doubted ones) are shown as their image, the cap `pageImages` starts there
